what_it_states: Scalar inputs and outputs (R), sensitivity |x-x'| <= s, objective = worst-case KL divergence sup D(P_{Y|X=x} || P_{Y|X=x'}) (large-composition surrogate), subject to a worst-case expected cost E[c(Y-x)|X=x] <= C with c satisfying Assumption 1 (positivity, symmetry, monotonicity, continuity, tail regularity c(x) ~ beta x^alpha). Theorem 1 (Appendix A, averaging over uniform shifts, Prokhorov, joint convexity and lower semicontinuity of KL, Lemma 1 conditioning increases divergence): additive mechanisms suffice, an optimal additive law exists, and any such law is absolutely continuous (Remark 1: any law with finite sup-shift KL is absolutely continuous). Definition 1 / Theorem 2 (Appendix B): quantized 'cactus' family with geometric tails, finite-dimensional convex program, shifts reducible to the grid {1/n,...,1}. Theorem 3 (Appendix C, Lemmas 2-6, smoothing by exp(-|x|^gamma) kernels): the cactus family approaches the optimal KL value. Numerical results: for quadratic cost the Gaussian is strictly suboptimal for this KL objective (Figure 2), moments-accountant and DP-SGD comparisons (Figures 3-5).
what_it_does_not_state: No pure epsilon-DP (or (epsilon,delta)-DP single-shot) optimum; no MSE minimization under a DP constraint (cost is a constraint, KL is the objective); no multidimensional or l1-diamond statement; no staircase selector; no mixed-cost all-law bound E||Z||_2^2 >= (2/3) inf E||Z||_1^2; no closed-form optimizer (KKT system stated as not solvable in closed form in a footnote); its absolute-continuity conclusion concerns finite-KL laws and does not address the pure-DP all-law problem.
